title: Construction and filtered abutment comparison for termwise hypercohomology pullback
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], let $K^\bullet$ and $L^\bullet$ be bounded-below complexes of abelian etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] on $X$ and $Y$, and let $u:f^{-1}K^\bullet\to L^\bullet$ be a morphism of complexes [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. For the hypercohomology spectral sequences [thm-sp-if-e1] of the global-sections functors on $X$ and $Y$, indexed as $E_1^{p,q}(X,K)=H^p(X_{\Et},K^q)$ and $E_1^{p,q}(Y,L)=H^p(Y_{\Et},L^q)$ with $q$ the filtration degree, the pair $(f,u)$ induces a morphism of spectral sequences [def-sp-spectral-sequence]. Its $E_1^{p,q}$ map is $H^p(X_{\Et},K^q)\xrightarrow{f^*}H^p(Y_{\Et},f^{-1}K^q)\xrightarrow{H^p(u^q)}H^p(Y_{\Et},L^q)$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. Its abutment map is the canonical map $H^n(X_{\Et},K^\bullet)\to H^n(Y_{\Et},L^\bullet)$ on derived global sections [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], and it preserves the finite decreasing filtrations by $q$ and commutes with the identifications $E_\infty^{p,q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^qH^{p+q}$ of [thm-sp-if-e1]. The presentations, spectral-sequence maps, stabilization bounds $R(X,K,q,n)$ and isomorphisms $E_r^{q,n-q}\cong\operatorname{gr}^q H^n(X,K)$ for $r\geq\max(1,R(X,K,q,n))$ can be chosen simultaneously for all bounded-below complexes. The canonical abutment map is $P_{f,u}^n=H^n(R\Gamma_X(\eta_f)\,;\,\lambda_f\,;\,R\Gamma_Y(u))$, where $\eta_f$ is the unit of $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$ and $\lambda_f:R\Gamma_X Rf_*\cong R\Gamma_Y$ is the Leray comparison. No identity or composition law is asserted.

proof.text: Choose Cartan--Eilenberg resolutions $I_K$ and $J_L$. Put $F=f^{-1}$, which is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact], and let $\phi:F(I_K)\to J_L$ be the lift of $u$ supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-eilenberg-functorial]. The filtered complexes whose spectral sequences occur in [thm-sp-if-e1] are $\Gamma(X,\operatorname{Tot} I_K)$ and $\Gamma(Y,\operatorname{Tot} J_L)$. The termwise unit from [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] gives $\Gamma(X,\operatorname{Tot} I_K)\to\Gamma(X,f_*f^{-1}\operatorname{Tot} I_K)=\Gamma(Y,f^{-1}\operatorname{Tot} I_K)$, and then $\Gamma(Y,\operatorname{Tot}\phi)$ gives a map to $\Gamma(Y,\operatorname{Tot}J_L)$. Both maps preserve the filtration by $q$ because they are termwise maps of the double complexes. Applying (c) of [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] and the identifications of [thm-sp-if-e1] produces the required morphism of spectral sequences.

source.place: Lemma Tag 015J and Remark Tag 015K; filtered-complex functoriality

proof.text: For each $q$, the $q$-th row of a Cartan--Eilenberg resolution is an injective resolution of $K^q$ by [thm-sp-if-e1], and a bounded-below complex of injectives is K-injective by [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Thus the $q$-graded piece of the global-section map in step 1 is $\Gamma(X,I^q)\to\Gamma(Y,f^{-1}I^q)\to\Gamma(Y,J^q)$. In the pullback recipe [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], choose a K-injective resolution $r:f^{-1}I^q\to J'$ and a map $\psi:J'\to J^q$ such that $\psi\circ r$ is homotopic to the row map; this is possible because $J^q$ is K-injective by [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions]. The map $\psi$ is a lift of $u^q$ in the sense of $H^p(\phi)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial]. Therefore the $E_1^{p,q}$ map is $H^p(u^q)\circ f^*$, with the displayed source and target identified by [thm-sp-if-e1] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

source.place: Lemma Tag 0EZM, proof via the two spectral sequences

proof.text: Apply the finite convergence and filtered-map comparison of [thm-sp-if-e1] and [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields]. The total comparison through K-injective resolutions identifies its homology map with the unit--Leray--u derived map [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Transport the image filtrations by the canonical comparison in [def-weil-pbc-termwise-hypercohomology-presentation]. Filtration-step maps commute with inclusions by monicity, and their maps on successive quotients are cokernel.map. Choose stable-page bounds and quotient identifications simultaneously so that the stable-page maps are these quotient maps.
